name: Fairfax Bridge (Washington)
facts: Built in 1921, the Fairfax Bridge was the highest steel arch in Washington at the time, spanning 250 feet above the Carbon River and linking the remote town of Fairfax to the rest of the state.

Its 494-foot length features a 240-foot three‑hinged braced rib steel arch, two 14‑foot towers, and a 17.4‑foot‑wide roadway resting on a Warren stiffening truss, a rare engineering design in the U.S.

After decades of service, the bridge was closed permanently in April 2025 due to corrosion, leaving the isolated area accessible only via locked logging roads and sparking a 2025 emergency bill to fund a replacement.
